Its generating function and pole coefficient follow by summing the recurrence and using λ²=(b−2)λ+4. The positive root lies between 2 and b and exceeds the magnitude of the negative root; squeezing between consecutive powers proves the arbitrary-cutoff order and density zero. Independently for the smaller cap, the same state pair has transitions (v+w,w), (v,v+w), (v,v) for digits 0,1,others, respectively. The resulting affine recurrence has quadratic t²−(b−1)t−2. Evaluating the enlarged-cap quadratic at that positive root ρ gives ρ−2>0. Binary cap three splits each digit into independent bits at powers j and j+1, giving [(1−z)(1−z²)]^(−1) and odd residues 0,1 mod 4. An independent truncated GF(2) product using shifted bitsets agrees for bases 3–12, both caps, all levels through five, and binary cap three through level 12.
